observe.title: Activity 3.1: Observe a Torchlight
observe.definition: A torchlight is a portable light source that uses electric cells (battery), a switch, wires, and a lamp or LED. When the switch is ON, the cells push electric current through the wires to the lamp/LED, making it glow so you can see in the dark.
observe.questionText: If we open the torchlight, what will we find inside?

cell.title: 🔋 Electric Cell
cell.content: An electric cell stores chemical energy and pushes electric charge from its positive (+) terminal to its negative (−) terminal when connected in a circuit. The metal cap is the positive terminal and the flat base is the negative terminal. When you connect wires from + to − through a lamp or LED, the cell supplies the energy that makes the lamp glow.

dc.title: Direct Current (DC)
dc.desc: Batteries provide DC electricity - current flows in one direction. Used in mobile phones, flashlights, and electric vehicles.

intro.title: Topic 3.4: Conductors & Insulators
intro.subtitle: Which materials let electricity pass through? Let's find out! 🔬
intro.conductorsDesc: Materials that allow electricity to flow
intro.testingDesc: Use a tester to identify materials

tester.title: ⚡ Conduction Tester
tester.subtitle: Test which materials conduct electricity!
tester.conductorsDesc: Materials that allow electricity to flow easily. Metals like copper, aluminum, and iron have free electrons that can move through the material, creating an electrical current.
tester.semiconductorsDesc: Materials with conductivity between conductors and insulators. Examples include graphite and silicon. Their conductivity can be controlled and is useful in electronics.
tester.insulatorsDesc: Materials that resist the flow of electricity. Rubber, plastic, wood, and glass have tightly bound electrons that don't move easily, preventing current flow and keeping us safe.
tester.touchInstructions1: Touch both free ends to the material
tester.touchInstructions2: to test if it conducts electricity
tester.buildStep1: Connect a cell and a lamp with wires
tester.howItWorksDesc: When we touch an object with both free wire ends:
tester.conductorResult: If lamp glows: Object is a CONDUCTOR
tester.insulatorResult: If lamp doesn't glow: Object is an INSULATOR
tester.tip1: Make sure the two free wires don't touch each other
tester.tip2: Touch both ends of the object being tested
tester.tip3: Hold for 1-2 seconds to observe the lamp

applicationsDetail.title: 🔌 Real-World Applications
applicationsDetail.intro: Conductors and insulators are essential in our daily lives. Let's explore how they are used in real-world applications!

conductor1.title: Electrical Wiring
conductor1.desc: Copper and aluminum wires carry electricity safely through our homes, powering lights, appliances, and devices.

conductor2.title: Light Bulbs
conductor2.desc: Metal filaments inside bulbs conduct electricity to produce light. The filament glows when current passes through it.

conductor3.title: Electronic Devices
conductor3.desc: Circuit boards use copper tracks to connect components in phones, computers, and tablets, allowing them to function.

conductor4.title: Electric Vehicles
conductor4.desc: Batteries and motors use metal conductors to power electric cars, buses, and bikes, making transportation cleaner.

conductor5.title: Power Transmission
conductor5.desc: High-voltage power lines use aluminum and steel conductors to transport electricity from power plants to cities.

insulator1.title: Safety Equipment
insulator1.desc: Rubber gloves, boots, and mats protect electricians from electric shocks by preventing current from passing through their bodies.

insulator2.title: Wire Coating
insulator2.desc: Plastic or rubber coating on electrical wires prevents short circuits and protects us from touching live wires.

insulator3.title: Building Materials
insulator3.desc: Wood, glass, and plastic are used in construction to prevent electrical accidents and provide structural support.

insulator4.title: Protective Gear
insulator4.desc: Insulating materials in tools and equipment keep workers safe when handling electrical systems and appliances.

insulator5.title: Packaging & Storage
insulator5.desc: Plastic and cardboard containers safely store electronic devices, preventing static electricity and damage.

applicationsDetail.takeaway1: Conductors allow electricity to flow, making them essential for powering devices and transmitting energy.
applicationsDetail.takeaway2: Insulators prevent electricity from flowing, protecting us from electric shocks and preventing accidents.
applicationsDetail.takeaway3: Both conductors and insulators work together to make electrical systems safe and functional in our daily lives.
